questions.question: What organization maintains the top 10 web security risks?
What header forces browsers to use HTTPS connections?
What algorithm family is recommended for password hashing?
What protocol provides delegated authorization?
What technique replaces sensitive data with tokens?
What attack exploits vulnerabilities through automated security testing?
What security mechanism validates input against expected patterns?
What principle grants minimum necessary access rights?
What cipher suite provides perfect forward secrecy?
What header prevents MIME type sniffing attacks?
A script saved in a comment field executes for every visitor. Classify this XSS.
questions.explanation: Stored XSS persists payloads in server data.

questions.question: A crafted URL's script reflects back in the response and executes once. Classify this XSS.
questions.explanation: Reflected XSS returns payloads within the response.

questions.question: What XSS variant executes when page JavaScript writes untrusted data into the DOM?
questions.explanation: DOM XSS runs entirely in client-side code.

questions.question: Which cookie attribute, set to Strict, helps prevent CSRF attacks?
What attack corrupts DNS records to redirect users to malicious sites?
questions.explanation: Spoofed DNS sends victims to attacker servers.

questions.question: A store adds a response header listing exactly which origins may serve scripts, neutralizing injected tag-based payloads. Which header is it?
questions.explanation: CSP whitelists permitted script/style sources, blocking injected third-party payloads.

questions.question: A form embeds a hidden random token verified on submission so forged cross-site requests are rejected. What is this anti-CSRF defense called?
questions.explanation: The synchronizer token pattern ties a per-session random token to each state-changing form.

questions.question: Attackers replay thousands of email/password pairs leaked from another breach against a login page, relying on password reuse. Which attack is this?
questions.explanation: Credential stuffing automates login attempts with breached credential pairs, exploiting reused passwords.

questions.question: A user changes the URL from /orders/1042 to /orders/1043 and views a stranger's invoice. What vulnerability class is this?
questions.explanation: IDOR/BOLA exposes objects via predictable identifiers without enforcing per-user authorization.

questions.question: A bank page must never render inside another site's iframe. Which legacy header enforces that framing policy?
questions.explanation: X-Frame-Options DENY/SAMEORIGIN prevents framing; modern CSP uses frame-ancestors.
